title: Large-scale study for the photocatalytic degradation of paracetamol using Fe2O3/TiO2 nanocomposite catalyst and CPC reactor under natural sunlight radiations
author: Khasawneh, Palaniandy, et al.

steps.title: Prepare synthetic wastewater
steps.instruction: Grind commercial Panadol tablets (each containing 500 mg paracetamol) and dissolve the required amount in deionized water to make 15 L of aqueous synthetic pharmaceutical wastewater; use only analytical‑grade chemicals.

steps.title: Adjust solution pH
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of the 15 L paracetamol solution to the desired value using 3 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or 3 M sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) solutions.

steps.title: Add photocatalyst and mix
steps.instruction: Add Fe₂O₃/TiO₂ nanocomposite catalyst at the dosage specified by the experimental design, then mix thoroughly to obtain a homogeneous suspension.

steps.title: Transfer to reactor and aerate
steps.instruction: Pour the homogeneous suspension into the CPC reactor tank and place stone aerators in the tank to keep catalyst nanoparticles suspended, increase dissolved oxygen, and maintain suspension homogeneity throughout treatment.

steps.title: Position reactor for sunlight
steps.instruction: Place the CPC reactor in an open area with direct sunlight and tilt the reactor platform to match the local latitude of Penang (5.4 °N) for maximum illumination.

steps.title: Circulate suspension at set flow
steps.instruction: Activate the horizontal centrifugal pump (MS Series) to circulate the suspension between the water tank and reactor tubes at a constant flow rate of 40 L/min; maintain this flow for the duration of the photocatalytic experiment.
